note: Evidence, never a quarantine list: no build, test run or CI step reads this file (scripts/test-diag-coverage.py enforces that), so an entry cannot skip, retry or excuse a test. A first failure is recorded with its signature and reruns; a clean rerun does not establish a root cause, and an entry stays nonreproduced until its explanation is shown.

failures.signature: AddressSanitizer use-after-poison inside RtlCreateHeap, reached from msvcrt.dll during process start, 0.11 s after launch and before any corpus input ran
failures.reruns: The immediate rerun passed; the next run of the same seed was clean.
failures.explanation: No input or Cerid frame is involved. Not explained.

failures.signature: Segmentation fault of the DX12 gate during the full parallel CTest run
failures.reruns: Run alone it then passed 5 of 5 and 20 of 20.
failures.explanation: No renderer or frame-cook code calls the CEIR plan or interpreter the batch changed. Not explained.

failures.lane: linux-clang-fuzz, linux-gcc-debug and linux-gcc-asan on this host's WSL2 guest (i9-14900K)
failures.target: crd-fuzz-perf-flight, crd-fuzz-perf-bundle, crd-fuzz-ceir-differential, crd-fuzz-ceir-text, crd-fuzz-ckir-binary and the plain corpus replays
failures.signature: Wild jumps with corrupted registers and locals; ASan SEGV writing address 4 in asan_annotate_live_range; a container overflow on a byte push_back had just marked usable; MallocAllocator's power-of-two check failing on the constant 8; once a silently wrong result in an unsanitized gcc build
failures.reruns: Every artifact replays clean (39 replays of the 13 control artifacts, 3 x 10,000 repetitions, 328,000 sequential runs); the rate rose from about one per 400,000 to one per 18,000 executions within an hour; native Windows loops and a known-answer probe stayed clean.
failures.explanation: Input-independent and seen with the container annotation off, outside libFuzzer and without a sanitizer, so the evidence points at this machine (CPU or WSL guest), not Cerid code. Not settled: the separating run on another machine is the user's item in DIAG.10a.

failures.target: lld-link of large test executables (thin LTO)
failures.signature: lld-link 20.1.8 crashes with 0xC0000005 or Illegal instruction while running LTO codegen of a module unrelated to the change; no source diagnostic
failures.reruns: Reproduced twice in isolation with two different crash types on the same module; a re-link sometimes links and sometimes crashes.
failures.explanation: A nondeterministic crash inside the linker's LTO code generation, not a defect of the linked code; every link since this note is retried at most twice and recorded.

failures.signature: 1 or 2 of the 15 ceridc cases failed, varying between runs, with a Windows sharing violation in a child ceridc process; serially all passed
failures.reruns: Varied between runs; reproduced under -j 4 and never serially.
failures.explanation: Four inspect cases redirected their child's report into the same file in one shared working directory. Each discovered case now gets its own working directory (crd_discover_tests CASE_DIRECTORIES).

failures.signature: One of two device replay cases failed once in a full parallel run; its output was not kept
failures.reruns: After the fix the 14 device cases passed 10 repeats at -j 16.
failures.explanation: Two cases wrote the same record file while CTest ran them as separate processes in one directory; the second now writes its own file. The shared file is the likely cause, not a reproduced one.
